slides.title: Geometric Deep Learning Models
slides.notes: Open by framing Chapter 05 as an architecture selection lecture. The important move is to stop naming layers first and instead ask what kind of domain carries the signal, what transformations should be respected, and which residual or visual check will reveal whether the promise is actually being kept.

slides.title: The Architecture Contract
slides.notes: Use this slide as the contract that every later model must satisfy. A geometric layer is not only a computation; it names a domain, an allowed transformation family, a local operation, and a readout. The final check column keeps the lecture grounded in executable evidence rather than vocabulary.

slides.title: Model-To-Domain Routing
slides.notes: Treat the routing diagram as a decision aid, not a taxonomy poster. Images route to grid convolutions because translations are meaningful. Graph data routes to message passing because labels are arbitrary. Point clouds, meshes, sets, and sequences each carry a different notion of locality and transformation.

slides.title: CNNs On Grids
slides.notes: Emphasize that convolution is the grid case of a local shared rule. The same stencil is applied at every pixel or lattice site, so translating the input should translate the response. The formula is less important than the commuting behavior that the notebook checks with a tiny signal.

slides.title: CNN Filters As Generators
slides.notes: Use the generated artifact as a microscope. The input, derivative filters, and averaging filter show that a CNN layer begins with small local measurements rather than global recognition. The displayed zero translation residual is the finite diagnostic tying the image panel to the equivariance claim.

slides.title: Group CNNs Add Transformation Channels
slides.notes: Explain group convolution by separating spatial motion from transformation channels. Rotating the input should not destroy the feature; it should move activation among orientation channels. The notebook artifact demonstrates this with a simple pattern whose ninety-degree rotation becomes a channel permutation.

slides.title: GNNs Respect Relabeling
slides.notes: Keep the graph drawing subordinate to the algebraic idea. Node names are bookkeeping, so relabeling every node should relabel the output in exactly the same way. Message passing achieves this by aggregating neighbor information through symmetric operations tied to the adjacency structure.

slides.title: Attention Builds A Soft Graph
slides.notes: Connect attention to graph neural networks without claiming they are identical. The attention matrix is a learned dense adjacency whose rows form probability weights. For sets, permutation behavior matters; for sequences, positional or temporal information is deliberately added because order carries meaning.

slides.title: Transformers: Set Core, Sequence Add-On
slides.notes: This slide should prevent a common confusion. Self-attention by itself treats tokens through pairwise compatibility and can be permutation equivariant. Sequence modeling becomes ordered only after position, time, or causal masking is injected. The architecture therefore exposes which geometry is built in and which is supplied.

slides.title: E(3) Message Passing
slides.notes: Present E(3) message passing as the point-cloud version of the same contract. Distances and scalar features can be invariant under rigid motion, while coordinate-like vectors must rotate and translate predictably. The notebook check preserves pairwise distances after a rigid transform, which is the minimal sanity test.

slides.title: Mesh CNNs Need Surface Neighborhoods
slides.notes: Meshes add a subtlety that ordinary grids hide: neighbors live on a surface, and local coordinates may change from face to face. A mesh CNN must choose a neighborhood, transport or align features, and pool across cells without pretending that the surface is a flat image grid.

slides.title: RNN And LSTM Time Geometry
slides.notes: Use the time visual to distinguish sequence geometry from set geometry. The recurrence shares a rule across positions, while LSTM-style gates decide how far information should persist. Dilated receptive fields and memory traces both show how architecture encodes assumptions about temporal scale.

slides.title: Residuals Make Claims Auditable
slides.notes: This is the verification slide. Each residual corresponds to a promise made earlier: CNN translation equivariance, group-channel permutation, GNN relabeling behavior, attention row normalization, E(3) distance preservation, and gate range. The numbers are small because the notebook deliberately isolates the mechanism.

slides.title: Locality And Scale
slides.notes: Stress that locality is not the same in every architecture. A convolutional stencil expands through depth, a GNN expands through graph hops, attention can connect every token immediately, and recurrent models expand through time. Pooling and readout then decide which information becomes invariant.

slides.title: What Changes And What Stays Fixed
slides.notes: Use the three columns as a vocabulary cleanup. Invariance means the answer should stay fixed, equivariance means the output should move in a predictable representation, and stability means small domain perturbations should not cause uncontrolled output changes. Many mistakes come from blending these requirements.

slides.title: Routing Case Studies
slides.notes: Read these examples as design reviews. A molecule is not just a graph if three-dimensional geometry matters. A mesh is not just a set if surface adjacency matters. Language is not just a set if word order matters. The right model is the one whose built-in geometry matches the task.

slides.title: Failure Modes To Catch Early
slides.notes: Make this slide practical. Overbuilding symmetry can erase useful orientation or order, while underbuilding symmetry forces the model to relearn coordinate conventions from data. Padding, graph construction, local frames, and positional encodings are all places where a good-looking architecture can quietly break its contract.

slides.title: Takeaways And Lab
slides.notes: Close by returning to the notebook lab. Students should perturb one geometric assumption, rerun the corresponding check, and explain the failure or preservation in domain language. The final habit is simple: choose the domain, name the transformation, inspect the visual, and keep the residual nearby.
